gaps.sentence: The castle ___ (restore) at present, so the east wing is closed to visitors.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + restored for work in progress now.

gaps.sentence: He had his wisdom tooth ___ (take out) yesterday morning.
gaps.explanation: Causative: had + his wisdom tooth + taken out. The particle 'out' stays with the participle.

gaps.sentence: The theatre ___ in 1897 and reopened last year.
gaps.explanation: A finished date (1897) takes past simple passive: was + built.

gaps.sentence: The escaped prisoner ___ (believe) to be hiding in the mountains.
gaps.explanation: Impersonal passive pattern: subject + is believed/said/reported + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: The match ___ (abandon) because of the storm, so we got a refund.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive with have to: had to be + past participle for past obligation.

gaps.sentence: The new stadium ___ by the end of the decade.
gaps.explanation: 'By the end of the decade' needs future perfect passive: will have been + completed. The stadium is completed by somebody.

gaps.sentence: Thousands of homes ___ (flood) when the river burst its banks.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + flooded. The cause (the river) is in the when-clause.

gaps.sentence: I couldn't use the meeting room because it ___ (clean) all morning.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous passive: was being + cleaned over a period in the past.
